cross_row_leads.note: P2372 (Pochinki-Yaroslavl) existence/duplicate risk. GEM's own ResearcherNotes on P2372 admit its route map was ORIGINALLY a literal copy of THIS row's (P0756 Pochinki-Gryazovets) map, later 'partially corrected' by deleting the last point. P0756's own route already legitimately crosses Yaroslavl Oblast and includes a Yaroslavskaya compressor station (per proektirovanie.gazprom.ru's 5-compressor-station list), so a naive digitizer could easily have mistaken a Yaroslavl waypoint on P0756 for a distinct Pochinki-Yaroslavl terminus. HOWEVER: proektirovanie.gazprom.ru's own encyclopedia page for Pochinki-Gryazovets explicitly names a separate pipeline object, 'газопровод Починки — Ярославль', stating that Pochinki-Gryazovets was partly built to allow maintenance/reconstruction on 'газопроводах Починки — Ярославль и Грязовец — КГМО' -- i.e. Gazprom's own literature treats Pochinki-Yaroslavl as a real, existing, physically distinct pipeline (likely an older/smaller line in a similar corridor), not merely a section name invented for P0756. This CUTS AGAINST a pure non-existence/duplicate finding. A construction-industry page (smu-vyborg.ru) separately labels a project as 'Pochinki-Gryazovets pipeline, section Pochinki-Yaroslavl, km 101.6-170.1', which muddies this further by using 'Pochinki-Yaroslavl' as an internal SECTION name of the P0756 project rather than a separate trunk -- this may be that same firm's imprecise labeling rather than authoritative naming. Net: existence of a genuine Pochinki-Yaroslavl pipeline is plausible but not cleanly confirmed with its own independent length/diameter/capacity specs; the residual map-duplication (GEM's own admission) is a real ATTRIBUTION/ROUTE-GEOMETRY risk regardless of the existence question. See P2372's own validity[] record for the disposition.
